sn47.43:1.2: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn47.43:1.3: “Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Uruvela on the bank of the river Nerañjara under the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree just after I became fully enlightened.
sn47.43:1.4: Then, while I was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in my mind thus:
sn47.43:1.5: ‘This is the one-way path for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation … as in §18 … that is, the four establishments of mindfulness.’
sn47.43:3.1: “Then, bhikkhus, Brahma Sahampati, having known with his own mind the reflection in my mind, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, disappeared from the brahma world and reappeared before me.
sn47.43:3.2: He arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined hands towards me in reverential salutation, and said to me:
sn47.43:3.3: ‘So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Fortunate One!
sn47.43:3.4: Venerable sir, this is the one-way path for the purification of beings … … that is, the four establishments of mindfulness.’
sn47.43:5.1: “This, bhikkhus, is what Brahma Sahampati said.
sn47.43:5.2: Having said this, he further said this:
sn47.43:6.1: “‘The seer of the destruction of birth, Compassionate,
sn47.43:6.3: By which in the past they crossed the flood,
sn47.43:6.4: By which they will cross and cross over now.’”
